tool.description: Compact structured catalog of playbooks (project and global scope) with trigger, effects, trust and shadowing. Call once per task when matching a user request to a playbook. Pass revision to skip the body when unchanged. Optional query (the task in one sentence): where the machine enabled decision-model ranking, adds an advisory ranked list, needs_playbook_p and covered_by; entries stay unchanged and your own matching still decides. fit: true adds to every entry that is not shadowed whether it can run in this project (ready, compatible, setup, trusted, needs_consent); playbook_adopt_report gives the full report. health.status held: the playbook refuses starts until a person clears it; tell the person, never retry. An unchanged answer lists held playbooks in held.

fit.description:
Add `fit` to each entry that is not shadowed: whether it can run in
this project (ready, compatible, setup items, trusted,
needs_consent). Not part of the revision.

query.description:
The task in one sentence (optional). Only when the machine enabled
decision-model catalog ranking: adds an advisory `ranked` list,
`needs_playbook_p` and `covered_by`; otherwise ignored.

revision.description:
Catalog revision known to the client. If it matches the current one,
the body is not returned (response `{ unchanged: true }`).

workspace.description: workspace_id of another workspace (spec 7). None - the current one.

tool.name: playbook_catalog

tool.description: Get the current status of a run, including liveness: `driver_alive` (null when no process claims the run), `node_times` with each node's start and the age and pid of its open attempt (plus `past_estimate`, true once an open attempt is running past its `expected_duration`), and the node status `lost` for a node whose attempt process is gone. Use `node_times` to tell a slow node from a stuck one, and `apb doctor --run <id>` for a full per-run diagnosis. `estimate` is what the run was expected to take at start; `budget` (when the run has one) gives the limits, what was spent and is left per dimension, and the node a budget pause holds the run before. The answer is large (every node output); to wait for a run to finish or need input, call run_wait instead of calling this repeatedly.

workspace.description: workspace_id of another workspace (spec 7). None - the current one.

tool.name: run_status
